source_text.body:
Plan then implement code changes with Copilot agent mode
A workflow where Copilot drafts a plan, and once approved via 'Start Implementation', Agent mode makes the changes automatically.
·
Apr 1, 2026
Done with
GH
GitHub Copilot
What they did
One commenter’s workflow was to use Copilot’s Plan mode for bigger changes so it first asked clarifying questions, then wrote a plan.md file for review. After the person approved it by clicking Start Implementation, Copilot switched into Agent mode and executed the plan by making code changes automatically; they also advised being specific and pointing it at files with #file.
How it went
The thread describes this as an effective way to handle large features while conserving paid requests, but it gives no concrete project example or measured result. Other commenters warned that request limits and context compaction could still interrupt runs.
Worth knowing
The clearest catch was cost control: several commenters said to treat premium requests as scarce and avoid wasting them by planning first and scoping context tightly.
Try it yourself
with
GitHub Copilot
Copy prompt
I want to [describe change, e.g. add pagination to the orders list in [repo or file]]. First write a step-by-step plan listing files you'll touch and how you'll test it, and wait for my approval. After I approve, switch to agent mode, make the changes, run [test command], and summarize what changed.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/GithubCopilot/comments/1sal7qf/thinking_about_moving_to_copilot_what_is_the_best
